In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of hyperoxia on the fatty acid content of rat lung microsome and mitochondria in vitamin E-supplemented rats compared to vitamin E-deficient rat lung microsome.
the effects of hyperoxia on lung fatty acid composition and the role of vitamin E in the protection against hyperoxic lung injury.
the effects of hyperoxia on lung fatty acid composition and the effects of vitamin E on lung fatty acid changes during hyperoxia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hyperoxic exposure does produce specific alterations in lung microsoma and mitochondrial membrane lipid fatty acid composition in the vitamin E-adequate animal.
vitamin E deficiency does not alter the changes occurring in the fatty acid composition in rat lung microsomal and mitochondrial lipids during an in vivo exposure to hyperoxia.
vitamin E deficiency increases the susceptibility of the lung to hyperoxic damage and that this damage occurs in the lung microsomes with the mitochondria being relatively unaffected by hyperoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hyperoxia causes a decrease in the amount of lung microsomes extractable in the vitamin E-sufficient animals with no change in the total amount of lung mitochondria extractable in the lung.
vitamin E-deficiency causes a decreased ability to produce PUFA and/or an increased peroxidation rate of PUFA in the lung microsomal fraction during a hyperoxic stress.
vitamin E deficiency causes a decrease in the amount of PUFA present in the lung microsomal fraction with the decrease being more severe after hyperoxia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin E-deficiency increases the susceptibility of lung membrane fatty acids to oxidative damage.
vitamin E deficiency does not affect the changes in lung fatty acid content occurring after hyperoxia, but does increase the amount of peroxidation of the PUFA present in lung microsome membranes.
hyperoxia does produce specific changes in fatty acid composition of lung microsomes with the greatest number of PUFAs affected occurring in the microsomes of vitamin E-deficient lungs.
